quote: Die complexe Multiplikation legt es {+nahe+} [-nach-] denjenigen Functionen zu fragen welche zu einem beliebigen Zahlkörper in der Weise zugehören wie die Exponentialfunction zum Körper der rationalen Functionen, und die elliptischen Modulfunctionen zum ima= ginären quadratischen Zahlkörper.
english: Complex multiplication suggests asking for those functions which belong to an arbitrary number field in the same way as the exponential function belongs to the field of rational functions, and the elliptic modular functions to the imaginary quadratic number field.
topic: A remark that giving ever new proofs of quadratic reciprocity is pointless, followed by the suggestion to seek functions belonging to arbitrary number fields as the exponential function belongs to the rationals and elliptic modular functions to imaginary quadratic fields.

triage.modern_statement: Hilbert's 12th problem, also called the extension of Kronecker's Jugendtraum. For an arbitrary number field K, find explicit transcendental functions whose special values (at algebraic or CM-type points) generate the maximal abelian extension of K, or all its abelian extensions. This would play the role that exp(2πiz) plays for Q, where roots of unity generate all abelian extensions (the Kronecker–Weber theorem). It would also play the role that elliptic modular functions, the j-function and Weber functions, play for imaginary quadratic fields through complex multiplication. In the note, 'Körper der rationalen Functionen' is almost certainly a slip for the field of rational numbers, which the 1900 problem names.
triage.answered_by: Partially answered. Kronecker and Weber, then Takagi and Hasse, handled Q and imaginary quadratic fields. Shimura and Taniyama (with Weil) extended this to CM fields around 1955 using abelian varieties with complex multiplication, though this gives only part of the class fields. Dasgupta and Kakde (arXiv 2021) gave a construction for totally real fields, but it uses p-adic integration (Brumer–Stark units) rather than the complex-analytic functions Hilbert had in mind. The general case is still open.

evidence.claim: Wikipedia describes Hilbert's 12th problem as the extension of the Kronecker–Weber theorem and complex multiplication to arbitrary number fields. It notes the problem is also called Kronecker's Jugendtraum and says the general case is still open.

Shimura extended the theory to CM fields. Wikipedia also notes that Hilbert's 1900 statement suggests, incorrectly, that elliptic modular function values alone generate the abelian extensions of imaginary quadratic fields.
Shimura–Taniyama–Weil (1955) proved results for CM fields using abelian varieties with complex multiplication. Their work covers only part of the class fields of a CM field.
Dasgupta and Kakde, 'Brumer–Stark Units and Hilbert's 12th Problem', give an unconditional solution for totally real fields. The method involves p-adic integration for infinitely many primes p.
Schappacher, 'On the History of Hilbert's Twelfth Problem: A Comedy of Errors', traces how the problem's motivation came from Kronecker's Jugendtraum and complex multiplication.

triage.why: The note matches the 12th problem as Hilbert published it in his 1900 Paris address. It has the same motivation (complex multiplication) and the same two model cases: the exponential function for the rationals and elliptic modular functions for imaginary quadratic fields. It also names the same goal of finding analogous functions for an arbitrary number field. This diary entry looks like an early version of that problem. The CM case (Shimura–Taniyama) and the totally real case (Dasgupta–Kakde, p-adically) have seen major progress, but sources say the general problem is still open. Research continues, including recent Dasgupta–Kakde work and approaches through Stark conjectures.
